extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, broadcasters, and public relations/communications professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for standard American journalism writing and usage aimed at reporters, editors, and PR/communications professionals; covers grammar, punctuation, capitalization, inclusive language, media law, digital security, and topical style chapters. The AP Stylebook is a living reference updated periodically with new entries and topical chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: General reference to American English grammar and reporting principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Stylebook offers a basic reference to American English grammar, punctuation, and principles of reporting, including many definitions and rules for usage as well as styles for capitalization, abbreviation, spelling, and numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the foundational authority for journalistic prose and many corporate communications; intended to standardize grammar, punctuation and usage across newsrooms and PR outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference section for reporters covering business and financial news including general knowledge of accounting, bankruptcy, mergers, and international bureaus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes explanations of different chapters of bankruptcy and other business-specific terminology and usage tailored for reporters covering financial topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sports Guidelines and Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes terminology, statistics, organization rules and guidelines commonly referenced by sports reporters, such as the correct way to spell and use basketball terminology like half-court pass, field goal and goal-tending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides sport-specific vocabulary, stat usage, and organizational conventions to ensure consistent sports coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guide to Punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: A specific guide on how to use punctuation in journalistic materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains rules regarding hyphens, commas, parentheses, quotations and other punctuation marks with journalistic usage examples and conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Briefing on Media Law
rubrics_metrics.description: An overview of legal issues and ethical expectations for those working in journalism, including the difference between slander and libel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains legal distinctions (e.g., slander is spoken; libel is written) and provides cautionary guidance for wording, source attribution, and defamation risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo captions (cutlines) formula
rubrics_metrics.description: The simple formula of what to include when writing a photo caption, usually called a cutline in newspapers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes what essential elements to include in a caption (who, what, when, where, why/how) to accompany images consistently and informatively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing Marks
rubrics_metrics.description: A key with editing symbols to assist the journalist with the proofreading process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard editing symbols are provided so copy editors and writers can communicate corrections efficiently in production workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Security
rubrics_metrics.description: A guide to protect journalists, their work, sources, online accounts, and avoid online harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers practical guidance on securing communications, protecting source information, and reducing online risks to journalists and their reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography / secondary references
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides second reference materials for information not included in the book; for example, it says to use Webster's New World College Dictionary as a reference after the AP Stylebook for spelling, style, usage and foreign geographic names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs users to authoritative secondary references for areas beyond AP entries; note that AP later switched its official dictionary to Merriam-Webster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive language — avoiding labels (e.g., 'illegal immigrant')
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalistic usage of 'illegal immigrant' was no longer sanctioned; the use of 'illegal' to describe a person became regulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of a wider AP move away from labeling people; guidance encourages avoiding dehumanizing or stigmatizing labels and to choose language that focuses on actions and legal status rather than identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive terminology — 'birthing people' and 'pregnant people'
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommends the use of 'birthing people' and 'pregnant people'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises inclusive alternatives to gendered terms where appropriate; later clarifications and updates refine recommended usage and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of singular they/them/their 'where possible'
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2022–2024 edition recommends 'where possible' usage of 'they/them/their' singular pronouns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports respecting individuals' pronoun choices and provides guidance on using singular 'they' in journalistic copy when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution on the word 'female' when describing women
rubrics_metrics.description: Cautions use of the word 'female' in the context of describing women, as some people object to emphasizing biology and reproductive capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages sensitivity to connotations of certain words and to choose descriptors that respect subjects' dignity and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of racial identifiers (capitalize Black; lowercase white)
rubrics_metrics.description: AP stylebook moved to capitalized Black and lowercase white.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies capitalization conventions for racial terms to reflect usage and editorial judgment; part of ongoing updates reflecting cultural and linguistic developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation of ethnic identifiers (removal of hyphen)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommends removal of the hyphen in Asian‑American, African-American, or Irish-American, citing hyphen removal as a correction of a long-standing microaggression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes orthographic changes to reflect contemporary sensibilities and to avoid implied separateness conveyed by hyphenation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polling and surveys guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes a chapter on polling and surveys (added in 2018).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides standards for reporting polls/surveys, including methodological caveats, sample descriptions, and attribution to help readers evaluate accuracy and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health and science chapter and guidance (2019)
rubrics_metrics.description: Health and science chapter debuts in 2019; guidance includes how to report on health, science and related terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives reporting conventions for scientific and medical topics, aiming to improve accuracy and public understanding in coverage of health and science issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical guidance for contested place names and official changes
rubrics_metrics.description: When a political or official renaming is contested (example: 'Gulf of America' vs 'Gulf of Mexico'), AP recommended using both names and noted that countries and bodies may not recognize the change; historical names may be retained where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises using both the new and historically recognized names when a change is not universally recognized and explains geopolitical/contextual rationale to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Living-document revision process
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries are regularly added or revised (annually or biennially depending on edition) to keep the Stylebook up to date with technological and cultural changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should consult the most recent edition or the online service for current guidance; the Stylebook documents additions/changes (e.g., new entries like 'Twitter', 'deepfake', 'cryptocurrency').

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical chapters added as needed (criminal justice, digital security, inclusive storytelling, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Stylebook adds topical chapters as issues emerge (examples: inclusive storytelling, criminal justice, digital security, polling, health and science).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that the Stylebook expands into subject-matter chapters to offer specialized guidance for reporting complex beats and topics.
